html:
The civil war of 83 to 82 BCE in which Sulla returned from the east and defeated the followers of the dead Gaius Marius, who held Rome.

Sulla had made peace with Mithridates in 85 BCE and landed at Brundisium in 83 BCE with his veteran legions. Ambitious young men joined him: Pompey, who raised three legions of his own, Crassus and Metellus Pius. Against him stood the consuls of the Marian party, Marius's son and many Samnites, who still hated Rome after the Social War.

Sulla beat the younger Marius at Sacriportus in 82 BCE and shut him up in Praeneste, where he later killed himself. The last fight came at the Battle of the Colline Gate, at the walls of Rome, in November 82 BCE. Sulla's own wing was pushed back, but Crassus won on the right.

Sulla then made himself dictator and began the proscriptions. Pompey was sent to clear the Marians out of Sicily and Africa. One Marian, Quintus Sertorius, escaped to Spain and kept the war going there as the Sertorian War.
sum: The civil war of 83 to 82 BCE in which Sulla returned from the east and defeated the followers of the dead Gaius Marius, who held Rome.
